title: Passive (form of be)
note: B1 · be agreement in passive frames · EVERY stem tense-forced (every/always/still vs yesterday/last/year) · will/must be · Match off · 2026-07-26 · RUE2 TRANSPLANT 2026-08-25: blocks+intro restored from rue2-grok-v1.0 (James-smoked, quality=good_draft); auto-authored bank superseded. · 2026-08-28 smoke: Quiz = form MC (correct be+pp · swapped number · be+lemma · bare pp). Type = fill that form. Use = active↔passive. Six inverted-question gaps rewritten as statements so the subject is never inside the gap (Were the lights turned / Was turned mix). · 2026-09-04 B1 loop: C20 the What-you-practise recap card cut (and the C4 it carried with it); B3 authored chips on all 48 items in the axis the note already specified — correct be+pp, swapped number, be+lemma, bare participle; D1 one explanation covered all 48 and each now names its own subject, its be form and its participle. A4's 31 candidates stand: a passive with a definite subject is where English forces `the`, and the Czech reflexive passive carries no demonstrative to add.

cards.title: What is the passive?
points: In the **active**, the subject **does** the action.
In the **passive**, the subject **receives** the action.

cards.title: Subject and object
points: Passive: the thing is the new subject
The old doer can go, or come back as **by someone**

cards.title: When and why we use it
points: Skip the doer when it would only be *someone / they / people*

cards.title: Form
points: **Past participle** = the form after *have*: *have **built***, *have **spoken***. Here it comes after *be*.
built, spoken, made, signed, grown…
Not now: *has been done* · *is being built* (later)
Passive = **be** + **past participle**.

cards.title: by + agent (optional)
points: Most passives have no *by*
If you always add *by someone*, you often don't need the passive

cards.title: Czech comparison

table.caption: Rough pairs (idea, not 1:1)
rows: Ukradli mi kolo. / Kolo mi ukradli.
These phones are made in Asia.
Tyhle telefony se vyrábějí v Asii.

points: se often ≈ English passive (process / general)
byl/byla/bylo + příčestí ≈ was/were + past participle
Active Czech (ukradli mi…) can still be passive English when the bike is the topic
Czech often uses se / -no/-to / or a different word order where English prefers be +
past participle.
Don’t translate word-for-word — match the idea (thing affected first).

cards.title: Active ↔ passive (same idea)

rows: They make these phones in Asia.
These phones are made in Asia.

points: Object of the active becomes subject of the passive.
Be takes the tense; main verb becomes past participle.

cards.title: Questions
points: **be** moves to the front
